newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Women's faces "source of corruption" - Afghan Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Women's faces "source of corruption" - Afghan Taleban.

text.p: An official in the Attorney General's office of Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban rulers said on Tuesday that women's faces are a source of corruption for men.
"The face of a woman is a source of corruption for men who are not related to them." said the official, who declined to give his name.
He was expounding on a point made by Attorney General Maulawi Jalauddin Shinwari during an interview with Reuters in Kabul.

"We consider that a woman should have her face covered when she goes outside, because the face is the point of attraction. If you read books, poets are always talking about the attractiveness of eyes, noses and lips," said Shinwari.
The Taleban have decreed that when women leave their houses they must wear the burqa, a shroud-like head-to-toe veil that leaves only a small hexagonal patch of gauze for the wearer to see out of.

The Taleban first appeared in Afghanistan more than two years ago and became the most powerful of several groups contending for power. They took over Kabul last September and now control most of the country.

Most of the Taleban are from southern Afghanistan, where it is a tradition that women should not work and should stay at home. The Taleban have given legal force to this tradition in the areas they control, though it has never been part of the northern Afghan way of life.
